leadText:
A Poké Fan (Japanese: だいすきクラブ Fan Club), formatted as Pokéfan prior to Pokémon X and Y, is a type of Pokémon Trainer that debuted in the Generation II games. They come in two varieties: middle-aged women with (outside of ) or a Pokémon magazine , and middle-aged men with small dressed in , , or outfits, or a bag of Pokémon-themed merchandise . Trainers of this class are members of the Pokémon Fan Club.

In Double Battles, two Poké Fans paired together are called a .

They raise many different cute that usually belong to the . The Pokémon of Poké Fans are notable for always holding a , Oran Berry, or Sitrus Berry, depending on the game. In the Generation V and Generation VI games, they may use Hyper Potions and Full Restores on injured Pokémon during battle.

===Pokémon Adventures===
====History====
===== =====
In Oh, It's Ho-Oh!, a male and female Poké Fan go towards the Indigo Plateau with their .

In The Last Battle XIII, a male and female Poké Fan appeared as two of the Trainers that lent their Pokémon for the final battle against the Masked Man.

===== =====
In As Luck Would Have It, Kirlia and Moving Past Milotic, has a Double Battle at the Battle Pike, against virtual male and female Poké Fans who use and .

===== =====
In Weavile Wobbles But It Won't Fall Down, a female Poké Fan and her son appeared amongst the people at the Safari Zone Gate.

===== =====
In Deprogramming Porygon-Z, a female Poké Fan was seen entering the Battle Castle with her .

===== =====
A male and a female Poké Fan appeared in An Odd Speech, listening to Ghetsis' speech.

===== =====
In Kangaskhan...Kangascan't, a male Poké Fan appeared at Santalune City with his son and their . Another male Poké Fan without a son walks past after she ran off from the others for easily trusting Viola.

A female Poké Fan with her son was seen in 's flashback in Pinsir Glares.

In Xerneas Gives, a female Poké Fan with her daughter appeared at Lumiose City.

==Trivia==
In all of the games, the species of the dolls accompanying the female Poké Fan sprite shown changes (progressing with , , , , , , , and ), but until Pokémon X and Y, the male Poké Fan sprite has always been shown holding a child in a or costume, as well as the Pokémon's icon imprinted onto their T-shirts.
Because the female Poké Fan sprite remains the same between Diamond, Pearl, and Platinum and HeartGold and SoulSilver, they are shown to have dolls in a region where Sudowoodo appears only once (and is apparently not well-known) and where Bonsly does not appear in the regional Pokédex.
The Poké Fan is voiced by Kaiji Tang in Pokémon Masters EX.
